n: Six documents from Monday. The first is a post from the research institute Ai2 about robots that handle objects. It releases a test of 307 videos marked by people and a training set of 3,000 videos from 300 simulated homes, and it says the trackers still struggle when a point is hidden for a long time. The second is from OpenAI and Cisco: open-source software that puts a temporary shield on a running Linux system while a permanent fix is prepared. The post says testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks, and it calls the software a first step. The third is from Google DeepMind. Teams of AI agents improved known quantum algorithms, and each result was proved with a formal proof checker. The post says running them would still demand more computing than the first error-corrected quantum computers are likely to provide. The fourth is from OpenAI's release notes: GPT-6.2 is reaching the chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise plans. The fifth is from Anthropic's platform notes: Claude Opus 4.5 is scheduled to retire from the API on January 22, 2027, and a beta option for eligible organizations sends encrypted copies of prompts and responses to a bucket in the customer's own cloud account. The sixth is a Hugging Face guide to testing AI agents. It cites an audit where accuracy varied by up to 29.9 percentage points when only the software around the model changed. What it means for your work: the strongest claims this week came with a way to check them. A proof, a test set marked by people, a published date. When a tool tells you it did something, ask what you could look at to track it yourself.
